content.intro: Coroutines enable cooperative suspension and resumption within a Lua thread; they are not operating-system threads. The host or caller determines when a coroutine runs and whether it is resumed again.

content_blocks.title: Work through the example
content_blocks.text: Read the small example, predict every output line, then run it locally with a compatible runtime. Run with the Lua 5.5 interpreter unless the example explicitly names a host API or another runtime. Keep the smallest reproducible case if the observed behavior differs.

content_blocks.code:
local worker = coroutine.create(function()
    local reply = coroutine.yield("waiting")
    return "received: " .. tostring(reply)
end)

local ok, message = coroutine.resume(worker)
print(ok, message)
local ok2, result = coroutine.resume(worker, "go")
print(ok2, result)
